faft: Prevent flashrom section file trampling. Before, the flashrom handler would dump section files such as RO_FRID directly into the temp dir, so calls to different handlers' new_image methods could trample on each other's data files. Now, the handlers use separate directories, and the directories are removed in deinit(). As a bonus, this also moves the updater's handlers into the same directory as the other updater files (/var/tmp/faft/autest), so they'll be removed during teardown. This will be particularly needed with a following change, since loading the Updater handlers lazily means they could trample on the Bios and Ec handlers' data in the middle of a test. BUG=b:139003282 TEST=Run firmware_Update*Version tests and any others that use Updater Change-Id: I6f24c6e2896ea16ca37e31332a740e4dcd4a3c50 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1747998 Tested-by: Dana Goyette <dgoyette@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Dana Goyette <dgoyette@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com>

shill: connection: Remove Binder Connection::Binder was previously used as a way of informing dependents when a Connection goes down. However, there is currently no code in Shill that actually needs this. The only Binder client is VPNService, but this usage is unnecessary. The lifetime of a Connection is controlled by Device, which will call SetConnection(nullptr) when removing an existing Connection, so VPNService can cleanly keep track of Connection removals without the use of Connection::Binder. Functionality will be added to VirtualDevice to map virtual devices onto physical devices. Doing this in Device rather than Connection allows for VirtualDevices to map to a physical Device even when the Device is not yet up (e.g. arc_wlan0 should still map to wlan0 even when we have not yet connected to a WiFiService). This also allows us to expose Device dependency information to the D-Bus interface (e.g. if we have both a cellular dongle and l2tp VPN, there is currently no clean way to determine which PPPDevice maps to which usage from the D-Bus interface).
